title: Sorts are not stable across partitions; ties come in partition order
verdict: `tie_order`: ties in an order that changes with the partitioning and between runs
description: A global sort range-partitions the rows and sorts each partition; equal keys keep the order they arrive in from the shuffle, which depends on the partitioning and on task timing. On one partition the sort keeps input order (`b`, `d` before `a`, `c`, `e`). After a 3-way shuffle the same query gave its ties in different orders on the folded and the codegen paths and between two runs of the probes, so a `LIMIT` on ties picks different rows.
reference: `tie_order`: any order of the ties, and any rows of a tie for a `fetch`. Every behaviour is allowed; sverify's Spark engine refuses plans that need a table's row order unless `tie_free=True`.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.
